prerequisites: Recommended: competencies from the modules Machine Learning, Introduction to Natural Language Processing, and Fundamentals of Statistics or Elementary Stochastics.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can explain the basic functioning of dialogue systems, voice assistants, and conversational systems.
Students can design implementation approaches for such systems.
Students can realize simple dialogue systems.
Students are able to apply scientific working methods in independently recognizing, formulating, and solving problems.

syllabus_topics: Architecture of dialogue systems, voice assistants, and conversational systems (chatbots)
Main components of dialogue systems and approaches to their implementation

assessment_methods.method: Weekly exercise assignments (at least 50% of points)
Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and orally present the solution to at least two of these assignments. The examination is either a written exam or an individual oral exam. Grading is on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science program.
bibliography: Jurafsky, Daniel, and James H. Martin. "Speech and Language Processing: An Introduction to Natural Language Processing, Computational Linguistics, and Speech Recognition."
